method: Rolling-origin model comparison with final holdout
interpretation: ETS(auto) had the lowest mean validation MAE (1.86); the runner-up was Theta (1.97). Final-holdout MAE for the selection: 1.67 against 2.8 for Seasonal naive. Validation MAE of Seasonal naive: 2.43.
assumptions: Regular series with the declared season and no missing periods
The training history's pattern continues over the horizon (no regime change)
Specifications are frozen on the first training slice, so later actuals cannot steer selection
not_done: No regressors, promotions or calendar effects (pool regressors, chapter 13 or 16 add them)
Conformal bands come from few origin residuals; chapter 17 gives a calibrated split with more

route_reasons: a regular series with enough history: the chapter 12 engine (smoothing, ARIMA, Theta, STL, LightGBM, combinations) at rolling origins

conformal: conformal_lower/upper are split-conformal bands at 80% from ETS(auto)'s absolute residuals at the selection origins, pooled across horizon steps (60 residuals, scaled per step); the guarantee assumes future errors resemble those at the origins, which a level shift breaks.
evaluation: 5 expanding origins spaced 12 steps apart select the model on mean MAE; the final 12 observations are scored once and never used for selection; the selection is refitted on all history. A model that loses to Seasonal naive at more than half the origins cannot be selected.
intervals: lower/upper are the ETS(auto) model's nominal 80% intervals; their coverage at the 5 selection origins was 80%. empirical_q* columns add signed residual quantiles by horizon step from those origins (5 residuals per step).
